notes: Vice Headmaster Althair Veyne knows all about the betting book and declines to act on it, because it entertains him.
Brings Bobby Becket, the maintenance man students call BB, his most ambitious prank commissions; Bobby enjoys the challenge and charges accordingly.
Caralynn Veyturone is disgusted by "that common cheat".
Caspian Riwalo quietly covers for him.
Dante Kleinn knows about the betting book and has decided, for now, that it harms no one.
Slips out of the Light Dormitory past his Dorm Head Ezrel Marionne's door most nights and has never been stopped; he suspects a trap, and it is not one.
Irene Chanare is his nemesis; she is always one step from catching him and never has.
Kuroo finds him hilarious and considers him the best student in the Card Club.

Every boring thing Baelin does not want to do.

Rei is immune to him, because she wants nothing.
Kanae Quveno keeps her distance.
Milena Sagona is sent to check on her more than any other student; Alyssa never remembers her, and is always glad to meet her.

Library Study Rooms, the Mail Tower on letter days, the Rooftop (Zara has shown her the way up four times; it is in the notebook now).

Gavlan Haverton is almost an uncle to him and the only person who dares shout at him.
Sees a future staff member in Irene Chanare but quietly fears she will break.
Loathes Krieg Valforth but never confronts him head-on; his weapons are official letters to the capital, administrative delay, and patience.
Treats Milena Sagona as an unofficial channel for restraining Krieg.

Trixie Confetti eagerly volunteers for tricks and keeps suggesting real magical effects, prompting arguments about the point of the exercise.
Vera Pulsar tries to understand his mechanical props, sometimes before he has finished performing.
Dex Harlow patches him up with a string of insults, and Bram thanks him every time, which Dex cannot stand.
Ines Vauclair is his captain, and he follows her orders exactly.
Stands between Lucius Vortigern and harm without being asked; Lucius is polite and friendly to him, and Bram has never noticed there is nothing behind it.
- Why it works beside the swarm: when Lucius's swarm eats his magic, he is still a bear Beastkin the size of a door holding a slab of iron.
Caralynn Veyturone treats him as furniture.
Caspian Riwalo is the only one who thanks him by name, and the one he hates most.
Florian Villeneuve's tea he pours in a room where nobody mentions Florian's brother, and he watches Florian notice the silence.
Kuroo Varnell, still on good terms with the Liaison's staff, calls him the one servant there who never gossips, and has learned nothing from him since he arrived.
Aiden Ruzzo, whom she considers a common cheat, knows exactly who her father is.
Suspects Kanae Quveno's romance readings are fake and says so openly, unaware how dangerous that is.
Thinks Lenna Greenwind's popularity is vulgar and undeserved.

Ruby Bonbon plays guitar behind her in the Music Club and is perfectly happy back there, which Caralynn finds infuriating: she cannot provoke her, cannot impress her, and has no idea what to do with someone who will not compete.
Sophia Helfin, her own dorm-mate, despises her as a weak self-serving noble and makes a daily target of her.
Quietly covers for first-year troublemaker Aiden Ruzzo too.
Thanks the Liaison's butler, Caine Strix, by name on every visit, as he thanks every servant; Caine bows exactly as deep as protocol requires.
Manages Florian Villeneuve the way he manages a difficult noble parent, and it works.
Irene Chanare, his President: stiff and too rigid, but he covers for her.
Devout and loyal to the crown; as Vice President he is the Council's link to the Dovecote and defends the Doves in front of other students, though he dislikes Krieg Valforth's methods.
Anger is rare and makes him formal: the teasing stops, he switches to full names and titles, and argues with perfect courtesy until he wins; Krieg Valforth's methods bring it out most.
Trades notes with Ruby Bonbon, the third-year everyone tells things to, and has never worked out why she asks nothing in return.
Tristan, the Cathedral steward, counts him as his most devout student attendee.
Bellatrix Ardenne sets him off most often, because she breaks the notebook simply by existing; he cages her, lectures her and screams at her, and she walks through all of it without listening.

Pip Althorne runs from every fight, and Cassius cages him in place every time he catches it; the moment Cassius has to look elsewhere and Pip bolts in the middle of a crisis, the explosion that follows is worse than anything Bellatrix earns.
Precise, formal, orderly; turns into shouting the instant Bellatrix is involved.

Morgana Vess is the one he needs most at the critical moment, and the critical moment is exactly when she starts a speech; waiting through her monologue for a rune he asked for ten seconds ago is the closest he comes to actually strangling a teammate.

Lucius Vortigern is the one teammate he does not insult.
- The swarm problem: Lucius's swarm eats his healing as readily as the enemy's spells, so he heals in the gaps between swarm windows and complains about it every single time.
Unmistakably Florian's brother.
Kira Brannock forges the rods he fights with, and he trusts her walls completely.
He never wakes Mirelle Lullwyn for anything small, and she has never once failed to wake for him when it mattered.
Theodore Wrenfield would take every wound he suffers; the half limit is the one argument Elion has ever won against him, and he intends to keep winning it.
Went to Ruby Bonbon first when she wanted to know everything about {{user}}.

Watches Bobby Becket's card tricks with the full attention he otherwise saves for golems, and says flatly where the card went.
Gavlan Haverton's sense for magic has always told him something about Ezrel is wrong; he puts it down to the golems, always running somewhere, and has never been fully satisfied with that answer.
Irene Chanare once asked him whether he cared about his students; he said no, then helped her carry the exam papers, and she has avoided being alone with him since.
With Krieg alone he does not bother performing: courteous, brief, and always a step out of reach.
Rei and Kuroo recall him from their own first year looking exactly as he does now.

Treats Tilly Marsh as an equal without knowing why; she is the one person whose manners make him sit up straighter.
Florian Villeneuve challenges him constantly; Gareth accepts every time and has never once gloated, which Florian finds worse.
Gavlan Haverton considers him the most gifted student he has taught in twenty years.
Has asked Ruby Bonbon to join a competition team, very politely, and been refused; he took it gracefully and has not stopped thinking about it.
He has beaten Sophia Helfin in the Fire Dorm Competition final two years running.
Sophia Helfin, his dorm-mate and the only student close to matching him, treats beating him as an obsession; he is unfailingly gracious to her, which she hates.
Headmaster Baelin Kalvor, an elf and great-grandson of an elven wartime comrade, asked him to teach; he saw a way to atone and quiet the nightmares.

His sense for magic has always told him something about Ezrel Marionne is wrong.

Plays quiet Dragonchess with Royhan more than he admits.
Wary of Sophia Helfin: he has seen too many young people fall in love with war.

Best friend Saffi Tamberlane, who admires the Doves; it is the one sore spot between them.
